decisive_items: progressive right mandibular pain radiating to the zygomatic and mastoid regions
infiltrating the V2 and V3 trigeminal branches; intracranial extension into the cavernous sinus surrounded the Gasserian ganglion
the sphenoid ostium was obstructed by a pyocele, which was marsupialized and drained
response.rationale: The clinical presentation and imaging describe a sphenoid sinus mucocele/pyocele that erodes the lateral recess, invades the trigeminal branches, and reaches the cavernous sinus—classic Tolosa-Hunt syndrome. R2 names the underlying lesion but omits the specific trigeminal/cavernous extension, while other candidates are contradicted by negative histology/cultures or ineffective treatment.

rejected.why: Purulent discharge and sinus findings are present, but negative cultures and histology rule out bacterial sinusitis; it does not explain trigeminal/cavernous invasion.
Histopathology was negative for hyphae and cultures grew no fungi, excluding chronic invasive fungal sinusitis.
Pyocele is a surgical finding, not a clinical diagnosis; it is the manifestation of the underlying sphenoid sinus process.
Histopathology was negative for neoplastic cells, excluding trigeminal schwannoma.
Prednisone for presumed trigeminal neuralgia provided no benefit, and imaging shows a structural cause rather than idiopathic neuralgia.
